description: Enterprise ATT&CK techniques and sub-techniques for adversary emulation
note: This is a subset of commonly used techniques. Full ATT&CK has 200+ techniques.

terms.label: T1595
terms.definition: Adversaries may execute active reconnaissance scans to gather information that can be used during targeting.

terms.label: T1595.001
terms.definition: Adversaries may scan victim IP blocks to gather information that can be used during targeting.

terms.label: T1595.002
terms.definition: Adversaries may scan victims for vulnerabilities that can be used during targeting.

terms.label: T1592
terms.definition: Adversaries may gather information about the victim's hosts that can be used during targeting.

terms.label: T1589
terms.definition: Adversaries may gather information about the victim's identity that can be used during targeting.

terms.label: T1590
terms.definition: Adversaries may gather information about the victim's networks that can be used during targeting.

terms.label: T1587
terms.definition: Adversaries may build capabilities that can be used during targeting.

terms.label: T1587.001
terms.definition: Adversaries may develop malware and malware components that can be used during targeting.

terms.label: T1588
terms.definition: Adversaries may buy and/or steal capabilities that can be used during targeting.

terms.label: T1583
terms.definition: Adversaries may buy, lease, or rent infrastructure that can be used during targeting.

terms.label: T1566
terms.definition: Adversaries may send phishing messages to gain access to victim systems.

terms.label: T1566.001
terms.definition: Adversaries may send spearphishing emails with a malicious attachment.

terms.label: T1566.002
terms.definition: Adversaries may send spearphishing emails with a malicious link.

terms.label: T1190
terms.definition: Adversaries may attempt to exploit a weakness in an Internet-facing host or system.

terms.label: T1133
terms.definition: Adversaries may leverage external-facing remote services to initially access a network.

terms.label: T1078
terms.definition: Adversaries may obtain and abuse credentials of existing accounts as a means of gaining Initial Access.

terms.label: T1078.001
terms.definition: Adversaries may obtain and abuse credentials of a default account.

terms.label: T1078.002
terms.definition: Adversaries may obtain and abuse credentials of a domain account.

terms.label: T1078.003
terms.definition: Adversaries may obtain and abuse credentials of a local account.

terms.label: T1059
terms.definition: Adversaries may abuse command and script interpreters to execute commands, scripts, or binaries.

terms.label: T1059.001
terms.definition: Adversaries may abuse PowerShell commands and scripts for execution.

terms.label: T1059.003
terms.definition: Adversaries may abuse the Windows command shell for execution.

terms.label: T1059.004
terms.definition: Adversaries may abuse Unix shell commands and scripts for execution.

terms.label: T1059.005
terms.definition: Adversaries may abuse Visual Basic for execution.

terms.label: T1059.006
terms.definition: Adversaries may abuse Python commands and scripts for execution.

terms.label: T1047
terms.definition: Adversaries may abuse Windows Management Instrumentation (WMI) to execute malicious commands.

terms.label: T1053
terms.definition: Adversaries may abuse task scheduling functionality to facilitate initial or recurring execution.

terms.label: T1053.005
terms.definition: Adversaries may abuse the Windows Task Scheduler to perform task scheduling for execution.

terms.label: T1543
terms.definition: Adversaries may create or modify system-level processes to repeatedly execute malicious payloads.

terms.label: T1543.003
terms.definition: Adversaries may create or modify Windows services to repeatedly execute malicious payloads.

terms.label: T1547
terms.definition: Adversaries may configure system settings to automatically execute a program during system boot or logon.

terms.label: T1547.001
terms.definition: Adversaries may achieve persistence by adding a program to a startup folder or referencing it with a Registry run key.

terms.label: T1548
terms.definition: Adversaries may circumvent mechanisms designed to control elevate privileges to gain higher-level permissions.

terms.label: T1548.002
terms.definition: Adversaries may bypass UAC mechanisms to elevate process privileges on system.

terms.label: T1134
terms.definition: Adversaries may modify access tokens to operate under a different user or system security context.

terms.label: T1055
terms.definition: Adversaries may inject code into processes in order to evade process-based defenses as well as possibly elevate privileges.

terms.label: T1055.001
terms.definition: Adversaries may inject dynamic-link libraries (DLLs) into processes in order to evade process-based defenses.

terms.label: T1070
terms.definition: Adversaries may delete or modify artifacts generated within systems to remove evidence of their presence.

terms.label: T1070.001
terms.definition: Adversaries may clear Windows Event Logs to hide the activity of an intrusion.

terms.label: T1562
terms.definition: Adversaries may maliciously modify components of a victim environment in order to hinder or disable defensive mechanisms.

terms.label: T1562.001
terms.definition: Adversaries may modify and/or disable security tools to avoid possible detection.

terms.label: T1003
terms.definition: Adversaries may attempt to dump credentials to obtain account login and credential material.

terms.label: T1003.001
terms.definition: Adversaries may attempt to access credential material stored in the process memory of the LSASS.

terms.label: T1003.002
terms.definition: Adversaries may attempt to extract credential material from the SAM database.

terms.label: T1003.003
terms.definition: Adversaries may attempt to access or create a copy of the Active Directory domain database NTDS.dit.

terms.label: T1003.006
terms.definition: Adversaries may attempt to access credentials and other sensitive information by abusing a Windows Domain Controller's API.

terms.label: T1110
terms.definition: Adversaries may use brute force techniques to gain access to accounts when passwords are unknown.

terms.label: T1110.001
terms.definition: Adversaries may guess passwords to attempt access to accounts.

terms.label: T1110.003
terms.definition: Adversaries may use a single or small list of commonly used passwords against many different accounts.

terms.label: T1558
terms.definition: Adversaries may attempt to subvert Kerberos authentication by stealing or forging Kerberos tickets.

terms.label: T1558.003
terms.definition: Adversaries may abuse a valid Kerberos ticket-granting ticket (TGT) or sniff network traffic to obtain a TGS.

terms.label: T1087
terms.definition: Adversaries may attempt to get a listing of valid accounts, usernames, or email addresses on a system or within a compromised environment.

terms.label: T1087.001
terms.definition: Adversaries may attempt to get a listing of local system accounts.

terms.label: T1087.002
terms.definition: Adversaries may attempt to get a listing of domain accounts.

terms.label: T1083
terms.definition: Adversaries may enumerate files and directories or may search in specific locations of a host or network share.

terms.label: T1046
terms.definition: Adversaries may attempt to get a listing of services running on remote hosts and local network infrastructure devices.

terms.label: T1057
terms.definition: Adversaries may attempt to get information about running processes on a system.

terms.label: T1082
terms.definition: An adversary may attempt to get detailed information about the operating system and hardware.

terms.label: T1016
terms.definition: Adversaries may look for details about the network configuration and settings.

terms.label: T1049
terms.definition: Adversaries may attempt to get a listing of network connections to or from the compromised system.

terms.label: T1021
terms.definition: Adversaries may use Valid Accounts to log into a service that accepts remote connections.

terms.label: T1021.001
terms.definition: Adversaries may use Valid Accounts to log into a computer using the Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP).

terms.label: T1021.002
terms.definition: Adversaries may use Valid Accounts to interact with a remote network share using SMB.

terms.label: T1021.003
terms.definition: Adversaries may use Valid Accounts to interact with remote machines by taking advantage of DCOM.

terms.label: T1021.004
terms.definition: Adversaries may use Valid Accounts to log into remote machines using Secure Shell (SSH).

terms.label: T1021.006
terms.definition: Adversaries may use Valid Accounts to interact with remote systems using WinRM.

terms.label: T1550
terms.definition: Adversaries may use alternate authentication material to move laterally within an environment.

terms.label: T1550.002
terms.definition: Adversaries may pass the hash using stolen password hashes to move laterally.

terms.label: T1550.003
terms.definition: Adversaries may pass the ticket using stolen Kerberos tickets to move laterally.

terms.label: T1560
terms.definition: Adversaries may compress and/or encrypt data that is collected prior to exfiltration.

terms.label: T1005
terms.definition: Adversaries may search local system sources to find files of interest and sensitive data.

terms.label: T1039
terms.definition: Adversaries may search network shares on computers they have compromised to find files of interest.

terms.label: T1113
terms.definition: Adversaries may attempt to take screen captures of the desktop to gather information.

terms.label: T1071
terms.definition: Adversaries may communicate using OSI application layer protocols to avoid detection.

terms.label: T1071.001
terms.definition: Adversaries may communicate using application layer protocols associated with web traffic.

terms.label: T1071.004
terms.definition: Adversaries may communicate using the DNS application layer protocol to avoid detection.

terms.label: T1105
terms.definition: Adversaries may transfer tools or other files from an external system into a compromised environment.

terms.label: T1572
terms.definition: Adversaries may tunnel network communications to and from a victim system within a separate protocol.

terms.label: T1041
terms.definition: Adversaries may steal data by exfiltrating it over an existing command and control channel.

terms.label: T1048
terms.definition: Adversaries may steal data by exfiltrating it over a different protocol than the existing C2 channel.

terms.label: T1567
terms.definition: Adversaries may use an existing, legitimate external Web service to exfiltrate data.

terms.label: T1486
terms.definition: Adversaries may encrypt data on target systems or on large numbers of systems to interrupt availability.

terms.label: T1489
terms.definition: Adversaries may stop or disable services on a system to render those services unavailable.

terms.label: T1490
terms.definition: Adversaries may delete or remove built-in data and turn off services designed to aid in recovery.

terms.label: T1529
terms.definition: Adversaries may shutdown/reboot systems to interrupt access to, or aid in the destruction of, those systems.
